summary: Go failed only the four §9.6 gating rows run.batch_target.{cmd,bat}_{space,nospace}_path, because CreateProcess runs .bat/.cmd through cmd.exe /c, which re-parses Go's CommandLineToArgvW quoting. Fix: run.Run now calls refuseTarget(path) after PATH resolution. On Windows it refuses any resolved path whose last component, after trimming trailing dots and spaces, has a .bat or .cmd extension (case-insensitive): exit 127, stderr message, CHILD_LAUNCH_FAILED. On Unix it is a no-op, so behaviour there is unchanged (darwin go test ok; harness 139/139 on darwin and linux-arm64). The new native test internal/run/batch_windows_test.go was cross-compiled and run on the host. It failed before the fix (90 cmd.exe executions: all casings, trailing-dot/space spellings, PATHEXT bare name) and passes after; it includes controls that ordinary executables still launch with exact argv. The unchanged Windows script was run for go only, 3 times (PS 5.1 x2, PS 7): exit 0, 94 rows, go 71/71 gating and host 4/4, verdicts identical across runs. The only verdict changes from the baseline are the four batch rows plus the non-gating run.cmd_metachar_argument (fail -> pass). REPORT.md has the 'Round 4 Windows (§9.6)' section with the full row table. Evidence is in tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-r4/x1b/go/. Host scratch was removed and no processes were left. Nothing was committed.
